content: The test image shows young corn plants that appear somewhat stunted with possible leaf discoloration/striping. Let me compare with reference images for the most likely candidates: Downy_mildew, Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma, Maize_streak_virus, and Stewarts_wilt.

## Analysis Summary

**Test image observations:**
- Young corn plants at early vegetative stage (~1-2 feet tall)
- Some leaves show pale/white parallel striping along their length
- Inner emerging leaves appear lighter/whiter than outer leaves
- Plants appear somewhat stunted relative to normal development
- No discrete lesion spots, no rust pustules, no discrete necrotic lesions visible

**Candidate comparison:**
- **Downy_mildew** ✓ — Reference images showed nearly identical young plants with white/pale parallel leaf striping, erect narrow leaves, plants at same growth stage. Matches the symptom description: "pale yellow or light-colored striping/mottling on leaves," "white parallel stripes alternating with green tissue," stunted plants
- **Stewarts_wilt** — Reference showed very tiny seedlings; test plants are larger. Requires visible streak lesions from flea beetle scars
- **Maize_streak_virus** — Reference showed much more dramatic, high-contrast yellow-white streaking; not matching
- **Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma** — Reference showed reddish-purple coloration and very advanced stunting; not matching
- **Gray_leaf_spot / NCLB / Anthracnose** — All require discrete lesion patches on mature leaves; not present

The white/pale coloration in the inner emerging leaves and overall plant habit at early growth stage aligns best with Downy_mildew, where newly emerging leaves show white parallel stripes due to systemic infection.
